confirmed.statement: S1: People were explicitly randomly assigned to ChatGPT or Google before writing their own vegetable-gardening advice; this supports individual, between-person assignment of a learning aid.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3 (index 2), Experiment 1, Methods, first paragraph and subsequent task instructions.

confirmed.statement: S1: The generative-AI arm used an in-house Qualtrics ChatGPT interface with unrestricted prompting, implemented with the OpenAI Chat Completion API and GPT-3.5-turbo; the reported mean was 2.06 prompts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3 (index 2), Experiment 1, Methods, ChatGPT-condition paragraph; p. 4 (index 3), Results, first paragraph; p. 9 (index 8), note c.

confirmed.statement: S1: The comparison was actual Google web search through the Custom Search JSON API, with ten links per page and repeat queries allowed, matching the other-aid arm.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3 (index 2), Experiment 1, Methods, Google-condition paragraph; p. 9 (index 8), note b.

confirmed.statement: S2: The methods explicitly report random assignment to two between-subjects conditions. Participants received search material before proceeding to a separate page to write their own advice.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6 (index 5), Experiment 2, Methods, first paragraph and paragraph beginning After completing the search task.

confirmed.statement: S2: Both arms supplied GPT-4o-generated material: a fixed 291-word, seven-suggestion summary versus six linked article variants retaining those facts. The form correctly records supplied AI material in different presentation configurations, rather than live ChatGPT versus ordinary web search.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6 (index 5), Experiment 2, Methods, paragraphs describing the simulated interfaces, GPT-4o summary, and six GPT-4o article variations.

confirmed.statement: S3: The methods explicitly report individual random assignment to two between-subjects conditions, implemented by computers with or without the Chrome AI Overview extension. Participants researched a healthier lifestyle before writing their own advice.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7 (index 6), Experiment 3, Methods, first paragraph and subsequent search and writing instructions.

confirmed.statement: S3: AI Overview is explicitly described as an LLM synthesis. Its users were instructed to read only that summary, while standard-Google users browsed links and were not shown the overview; no underlying model is named.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7 (index 6), final paragraph of Experiment 2 Discussion and Experiment 3 Methods, search instructions.

confirmed.statement: S4: Each recipient evaluated one randomly selected advice text from each S3 arm in explicitly randomized order. This randomized within-person evaluation did not assign AI assistance for recipients to produce their own work, exactly as the form records.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8 (index 7), Experiment 4, Method, first paragraph, especially the sentences beginning After reading this cover story and Participants were blind.

confirmed.statement: S5: The first supplementary replication explicitly randomly assigned participants to the same LLM or web-search conditions as Experiment 1 or a third LLM-plus-real-time-links condition. That explicit cross-reference supports the recorded open-chat role; the replication model is not separately named.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5 (index 4), Experiment 1, Discussion, paragraph beginning We also note; p. 3 (index 2), Experiment 1, Methods, interactive ChatGPT instructions.

confirmed.statement: S5: The reported 26% link-clicking figure belongs to the LLM condition augmented by real-time web links, as recorded in its arm description.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5 (index 4), Experiment 1, Discussion, supplementary-replications paragraph.

confirmed.statement: S1, S2, S4, and S5 are explicitly described as preregistered. The saved article does not identify Experiment 3 as preregistered, consistent with its not_stated field.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3 (index 2), Empirical analysis and Experiment 1 Methods; p. 5 (index 4), Experiment 1 Discussion; p. 6 (index 5), Experiment 2 Methods; p. 7 (index 6), Experiment 3 Methods; p. 8 (index 7), Experiment 4 Method.

confirmed.statement: S1-S3 describe writing after the search stage but do not establish removal of access to the learning tool or material during writing. The form appropriately leaves that access unresolved; the writer comparisons are between people, so randomized condition order is not required.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3 (index 2), Experiment 1 Methods; p. 6 (index 5), Experiment 2 Methods; p. 7 (index 6), Experiment 3 Methods; creativity-codebook.md, section 3, criterion 1.

confirmed.statement: S6 and S7 are briefly described as preregistered replications without study-specific random-assignment or condition-order statements in the saved document. The form does not assert randomization for either.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5 (index 4), Experiment 1 Discussion, second supplementary replication; p. 8 (index 7), Experiment 4 Results, conceptual-replication sentence.

confirmed.statement: Review coverage: all 398 markdown lines, including notes and references, were read, and the assignment passages were independently extracted from the PDF. The separate supplement is not included in the saved PDF or adjacent files; Europe PMC and publisher retrieval both failed with WinError 10013, so no supplement-only details were assumed.
confirmed.locator: Saved markdown lines 1-398; PDF p. 10 (index 9), Supplementary Material and its link annotation; retrieval attempts at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12560091/fullTextXML and https://academic.oup.com/pnasnexus/article-lookup/doi/10.1093/pnasnexus/pgaf316.

summary: The PDF supports randomized AI assistance in S1-S3 and S5, so criterion 1 holds. The form correctly distinguishes S2’s two AI-generated formats and S4’s randomized recipient evaluations; the separate supplement was inaccessible.
